outcome: functional recovery (measured by modified Rankin Scale [mRS])
cohort: The cohort consisted of 22 eclamptic women diagnosed with malignant posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) with or without intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH).
finding: Eclamptic women with malignant PRES and intracerebral hemorrhage can achieve long-term functional recovery comparable to those without hemorrhagic transformation through timely surgical intervention, despite worse initial presentation.
